title: 第21章：出路
novel_title: 穿越两界，我在80年代当倒爷
content_zh:
马超神色沉稳，不卑不亢，没有丝毫躲闪和推诿。

    “大姑，大姑父，我今天专程过来，就是为了这笔欠款的。”

    他语气平和，条理清晰，缓缓道出前因后果。从前父亲重病卧床，家里一穷二白，实在没有能力还债，并非有意拖欠赖账。如今他能自力更生、做点小生意赚钱，自然不会再拖着这笔旧账。

    一番话情理兼顾，不卑微、不辩解，坦荡又诚恳。大姑父心里也清楚马家过往的难处，知道马超踏实懂事，并非无赖之人，脸上的阴沉戾气，渐渐消散了大半，紧绷的肩膀也悄悄放松了些许。

    屋里一时安静下来，只剩几人的呼吸声。

    见气氛彻底缓和下来，马超不再拖沓，伸手揣进兜里，摸出一沓整齐叠好的零钱。他低头认真数了两遍，不多不少，整整五十六块，随后抬手，稳稳朝着大姑父递去。

    见气氛缓和下来，马超不再犹豫，直接掏出钱，熟练数出五十六块，伸手就要递过去。

    大姑见状脸色骤变，几乎是下意识快步上前，伸手死死按住了马超的手背，用力将他递钱的手往回推。

    她眼神慌乱又柔软，带着浓浓的人情暖意，看着马超低声阻拦：“小超，这钱不能还。当初这笔钱，是我借给你爸治病的救命钱，我从没打算催你还。”

    说完，她下意识偏过头，目光落在一旁的李军身上。看着儿子满脸失落、眼底藏着焦急与无助的模样，她眼底闪过浓烈的愧疚和挣扎，眼神飘忽不定，心里又悔又难受。

    短暂犹豫后，她重新转回目光看向马超，原本慌乱闪烁的眼神慢慢沉淀下来，变得格外坚定。她知道马家日子刚有起色，不想再让马超背负这份旧债压力。

    “真的不能还。”大姑语气掷地有声，态度格外坚决。

    马超看着大姑真诚又为难的神色，心中了然她的顾虑，却依旧没有收回手。他眼底坦荡笃定，语气格外坚决，轻轻挣开大姑的手，把钱往前递了递。

    “大姑，我知道你心疼我，想着当年是帮我家救命的钱，不想让我还。”

    “但人情归人情，账目归账目。当年我爸重病，家里走投无路，是你们这五十六块解了燃眉之急，这份恩情我记一辈子。可也正因为这笔钱牵扯太久，两家心里都压着事。”

    “欠债还钱，天经地义。我不能一直揣着旧账过日子，也不能让你们因为我家的旧债，耽误了军子哥的前程。”

    马超目光诚恳，扫过神色动容的大姑、眼神松动的大姑父，还有一旁默默站着、满脸复杂的李军，语气笃定无比：“大姑，我再说一次，我现在真的不一样了。我有靠谱门路挣钱，不用再熬苦日子，这点钱对我来说不算负担。”

    他轻轻将钱塞到大姑父手里，彻底了结这块心病，随后认真开口：“我今天专程过来，还清旧账是其一，最主要的，是想找一条正经生意路子，踏踏实实赚钱，以后不仅能顾好自家，也能帮衬亲戚。”

    大姑父看着眼前褪去青涩、沉稳笃定的马超，眼底多了几分认可和好奇，沉声问道：“你有什么门路？这年头，乡下挣钱最难，正经生意更是不好做。”

    马超顺势说道，“大姑父，你在供销社上班，见识广、门路多，现在市面上紧俏物资稀缺，这点没错吧？”
content_en:
Ma Chao looked calm, neither humble nor arrogant, without any evasion or shirk.

    "Auntie, uncle, I made a special trip here today just for this debt."

    His tone was calm and clear, and he slowly explained the cause and effect. Once upon a time, my father was seriously ill and bedridden, and the family was very poor. He really had no ability to repay his debts, and he did not intend to default on his debts. Now that he can be self-reliant and start a small business to make money, he will naturally no longer drag this old debt with him.

    What he said was both reasonable and reasonable, not humble or defensive, but frank and sincere. The eldest uncle was also aware of the past difficulties of the Ma family, and knew that Ma Chao was down-to-earth and sensible, not a scoundrel. The gloomy and aggressive look on his face gradually dissipated for the most part, and his tense shoulders quietly relaxed a little.

    The room fell silent for a moment, except for the sound of a few people breathing.

    Seeing that the atmosphere had completely calmed down, Ma Chao stopped procrastinating, put his hand into his pocket, and took out a stack of neatly folded change. He lowered his head and counted it carefully twice, no more, no less, a total of fifty-six yuan. Then he raised his hand and handed it steadily towards his uncle.

    Seeing that the atmosphere had calmed down, Ma Chao no longer hesitated and took out the money. He counted fifty-six yuan skillfully and reached out to hand it over.

    Upon seeing this, the aunt's face suddenly changed, and she stepped forward almost subconsciously, stretched out her hand to firmly hold the back of Ma Chao's hand, and pushed back the hand that handed him the money.

    Her eyes were panicked and soft, with a strong sense of human warmth. She looked at Ma Chao and stopped him in a low voice: "Xiao Chao, you can't pay back this money. This money was originally life-saving money I lent to your father for medical treatment. I never planned to force you to pay it back."

    After speaking, she subconsciously turned her head and her eyes fell on Li Jun beside her. Seeing her son's face full of loss, with anxiety and helplessness hidden in his eyes, strong guilt and struggle flashed through her eyes, her eyes were erratic, and she felt regretful and uncomfortable in her heart.

    After a brief hesitation, she turned her gaze back to Ma Chao. The originally flashing eyes slowly settled down and became particularly determined. She knew that the Ma family's life had just improved, and she didn't want Ma Chao to bear the pressure of this old debt again.

    "I really can't pay it back." The aunt said loudly and her attitude was particularly firm.

    Ma Chao looked at his aunt's sincere and embarrassed expression, and understood her concerns, but still did not take back his hand. His eyes were magnanimous and determined, and his tone was particularly firm. He gently broke away from his aunt's hand and handed the money forward.

    "Auntie, I know you feel sorry for me. You think you saved my family's life back then, and you don't want me to pay it back."

    "But favors belong to favors, and accounts belong to accounts. When my father was seriously ill and the family was desperate, it was your fifty-six yuan that solved the urgent need. I will remember this kindness for the rest of my life. But because this money has been involved for so long, both families are worried."

    "It's only natural to pay back debts. I can't live with old debts all the time, and I can't let you delay Brother Jun's future because of my family's old debts."

    Ma Chao's eyes were sincere as he glanced at the moved aunt, the slack-eyed uncle, and Li Jun, who was standing silently with a complicated face. He said in a very determined tone: "Aunt, let me say it again, I am really different now. I have a reliable way to make money, and I don't have to live a hard life anymore. This little money is not a burden to me."

    He gently put the money into his eldest uncle's hand, completely putting an end to this worry, and then said seriously: "I made a special trip here today to pay off old debts. The most important thing is to find a serious business path and make money in a down-to-earth way. In the future, I can not only take care of myself, but also help my relatives."

    The eldest uncle looked at Ma Chao, who had lost all his youthfulness and was now calm and determined. There was a bit more recognition and curiosity in his eyes, and he asked in a deep voice: "What opportunities do you have? These days, it is the most difficult to make money in the countryside, and it is even harder to do serious business."

    Ma Chao took advantage of the situation and said, "Uncle, you work in a supply and marketing cooperative. You have broad knowledge and many connections. Nowadays, in-demand materials are scarce in the market. Isn't this true?"
